issue.title: BUG: Windows fatal exception: access violation in .core.algorithms.safe_sort() with Python 3.15
issue.body:
### Pandas version checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.

- [ ] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [main branch](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/getting_started/install.html#installing-the-development-version-of-pandas) of pandas.


### Reproducible Example

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from pandas.core.algorithms import safe_sort

values = np.array(["c", "a", "b"])
result = safe_sort(values)
print(result)

idx = pd.MultiIndex.from_product(
    [
        ["foo1", "foo2", "foo3", "bar4", "bar5", "bar6"],
        [2000, 2010, 2020, 2030, 2040, 2050],
    ],
    names=["t", "y"],
)
print(idx)
```

### Issue Description

This error appears to only happen on Windows (specifically, on the [Github Actions `windows-latest` runner image](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/main/images/windows/Windows2025-VS2026-Readme.md)) with Python 3.15. It does not occur with Python 3.14 through 3.11 and otherwise identical code/OS.

I specifically see the error in Github Actions jobs like [this one](https://github.com/khaeru/genno/actions/runs/38905726556/job/116988687551) as part of khaeru/genno#204. The `pd.show_versions()` output below is from such a job. (I am unable to test or reproduce this directly as I do not have access to any Windows system.) Two specific ways that safe_sort() is reached within my code include MultiIndex.from_product() (as in the MWE) and DataFrame.set_index(). I do not see similar errors arising from any other cause, or any other piece of pandas code.

I searched for issues about (a) Python 3.15 support and (b) safe_sort(), and found #66740 but nothing else.

### Expected Behavior

No fatal exception. On other OS/Python version combinations, the code outputs:
```
['a' 'b' 'c']
MultiIndex([('foo1', 2000),
            ...
            ('bar6', 2050)],
           names=['t', 'y'])
```
